neighbours.label: subshell/orbital letters (s, p, d, f) and constants' digits in chemistry and physics text
fire: Lanthanides are the elements in which electrons fill the 4f orbitals.
The transition metals occupy the d-block in the middle of the table.
After the 4s orbital, electrons begin filling the 3d orbital.
Orbitals are labelled by letters: s, p, d, and f, by shape.
Uranium belongs to the f-block, below the main body of the table.
The configuration of iron is [Ar] 3d6 4s2 in its ground state.
Each p subshell holds up to six electrons in three orbitals.
Its valence electrons sit in a half-filled 5f subshell.
quiet: Lanthanides are soft metals that tarnish quickly when left in air.
The transition metals are mostly hard, shiny and good conductors.
After the reaction, the solution slowly turns a pale blue colour.
Orbitals describe where an electron is most likely to be found.
Uranium is mined in Canada, Kazakhstan and Australia today.
Iron rusts when it is exposed to both oxygen and water for long.
Each element has a unique number of protons in its nucleus.
Its outer electrons make it react easily with halogens.
